about.title: Orange Cove Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Orange Cove's economy runs on agriculture, packing houses, and the trucking that moves produce along Hills Valley Road, Anchor Avenue, American Avenue, and Serna Avenue. That mix means workers face a wide range of on-the-job risks, from equipment accidents in packing facilities to injuries suffered while driving or loading near these busier corridors. Under California law, workers' compensation is usually the exclusive way to recover from your employer no matter who was at fault, but that's not the whole story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may also have a separate claim against that third party. Sorting out which route — or both — applies to your situation takes a careful look at how the injury happened. LawProactive doesn't provide legal advice ourselves; instead, we connect injured workers in Orange Cove with an independent attorney who can review the details and explain your options, free of charge and with no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Only Option
items.desc: California generally makes workers' compensation the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be held separately liable. An attorney can help determine if your case involves more than one path to recovery.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California law generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your workers' comp claim, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and Third-Party Claims Have Their Own Clock
items.desc: Employers cannot legally retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If a third party is involved, that separate claim generally must be filed within two years, so timing counts.

items.question: I was hurt on a farm job near Orange Cove — is that covered by workers' comp?
items.answer: Most agricultural employers in California are required to carry workers' compensation coverage, so on-the-job injuries are typically covered regardless of fault. If equipment failure, a subcontractor, or another company's negligence played a role, you may also have a separate third-party claim worth exploring. An independent attorney can review your specific work situation to clarify your options.

items.question: Can I be fired for reporting a workplace injury in Orange Cove?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits employer retaliation against workers who report injuries or file workers' compensation claims. If you believe you've faced retaliation, that's something an attorney can look into separately from your injury claim.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work along Anchor Avenue or American Avenue?
items.answer: If you were injured in a vehicle collision while performing work duties, workers' compensation generally applies against your employer, but the other driver or a vehicle manufacturer could also be liable through a separate third-party claim. Because that type of claim carries its own two-year deadline, it helps to have both angles reviewed early. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who handles this kind of overlap.
